prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1246; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in the right lane of the northbound frontage road near Pearland when the rear of the vehicle was struck by Driver 2, whose vehicle was traveling at a speed the officer estimated as moderate for the conditions. Driver 1 reported pain in the right shoulder and said the impact pushed the vehicle forward with considerable force. The officer observed rear crush damage consistent with the described impact, and the overall pattern of damage to the bumper, trunk and taillight assembly matched what the drivers described. Photographs taken at the scene confirm the general position of both vehicles and the visible damage, though no independent witness was located who saw the collision occur. Driver 2 stated that the brakes were applied late due to distraction. A Passenger was present in the front seat of Driver 1's vehicle, but Driver 1 was not entirely certain of the seating position at the moment of impact and the passenger's account was brief. Driver 1 reported no prior damage to the vehicle, and the officer found no evidence of earlier repairs. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved.
